character_facts: Othon von Salza abandoned pure martial pursuits in favor of weapons development.
Othon became stronger and more energized after mutilation, according to the narrator.
Othon is characterized as cruel and solitary.
Othon exercised domination over Iku-Itta's daughters and demanded silence from them.
Iku-Itta is a loyal slave in Othon's household, as described by the narration.
characters_present: Narrator represented by a small monitor/speaker device
continuity_links: This page links Othon von Salza directly to the lineage of the current Metabaron.
It presents the origins of Metabaronic weapon development as part of the family history.
It ties Othon's personal transformation to the later built environment of Castaka on Okkar.
dialogue_meaning: The speaker frames this page as foundational backstory needed to understand later events.
The narration explains that Othon redirected his life from martial discipline into weapons development.
It states that mutilation psychologically and physically hardened Othon, making him more violent and isolated.
It describes his household arrangement with Iku-Itta's daughters as one of enforced silence and obedience.
It concludes that Othon used machine power to remake both the land and the family fortress on Okkar.
locations: Interior chamber with Othon, the women, and a servant
lore_facts: Othon von Salza is the great ancestor of the current Metabaron.
Early Metabaronic weapons were developed and constructed with Othon's wealth.
Othon's mutilation is presented as a major turning point in his life.
Iku-Itta is explicitly called Othon's slave.
Iku-Itta had daughters who were involved in Othon's household and sexual life.
Castaka is a fortress located on the planet Okkar.
Castaka was transformed from a rural fortress into a maxi-protonic tower.
Othon commanded an army of machines.
plot_events: A narrator says the story must be told from the beginning because later events have many causes.
Othon von Salza, identified as an ancestor of the current Metabaron, turns away from martial arts and invests his fortune in creating early Metabaronic weapons.
After suffering mutilation, Othon's rage and suffering intensify his strength and energy, changing him into a cruel, solitary warrior.
Othon is shown fighting and destroying machines in violent combat.
Othon continues taking the daughters of his slave Iku-Itta as sexual partners under a condition of total silence.
Using an army of machines, Othon transforms the rural Castaka fortress on the planet Okkar into a massive tower-city.
uncertainties: The narrator's exact identity is unclear; only a small monitor-like speaking device is shown.
Some proper nouns may be difficult to verify from the image alone, but they appear to read as Othon von Salza, Iku-Itta, Okkar, and Castaka.
visual_summary: A narration-heavy page presents the backstory of Othon von Salza. A small monitor-headed speaker introduces the account. Large panels show Othon battling machines, a close-up of his enraged face, a scene of him reclining with two silent women and a servant, and a towering fortress-city rising from a devastated landscape.
